column5: There's a page in my notebook I didn't write.
And it's warning me about myself.
I'm Mark. Seven days ago, Chicago went dark.
Every door got a red X.
Except mine.
Last night, a voice under the street said my name.
Then it whispered,
Don't get in the trucks.
I lifted the grate.
A rusty ladder dropped into pure black.
Mrs. Alvarez grabbed my arm.
If we go down there, we don't come back up.
Behind us, an engine started.
The last truck.
Its headlights swung into the alley.
We climbed down.
The tunnel smelled like smoke and wet metal.
Candles flickered on the walls.
And there were people. Dozens of them.
Kids. Old men. A nurse still in her scrubs.
Then a woman stepped out of the dark.
She wore a gray coat. The same one the man at my door had on.
Everyone they took to Wrigley never came back.
You're on their list because of what you saw on day one.
I didn't see anything on day one.
She didn't answer. She just pointed at my notebook.
I opened it.
The first page wasn't in my handwriting.
Mark. You already forgot once. Don't let them make you forget again.
And at the bottom, there was a date.
Tomorrow's.
